_comment: The lifecycle of a render template (CAP-TPL-008, ADR-042 decision 3). The same engine, the same segregation of duties and the same signature gate a label passes through - because a template determines what a patient reads, and approving one is a regulatory act with a named accountable person behind it. Its states are its own: a label is superseded by a newer version and a template is retired when it should no longer be used, and a template has no per-market approval at all.
name: render-template

transitions._comment: Signed, and segregated from whoever wrote it - the same two conditions a label's approval carries, for the same reason. Somebody signs to say this is fit to shape what patients read, and it is not the person who shaped it.
Retiring an approved template is signed too. Renders already filed with it stay valid and stay reproducible - retiring says nothing new may be rendered with it, which is a decision somebody owns.
